incidents.victim: US water, energy and government utilities
incidents.attacker: Iran — IRGC-linked industrial control system actors
incidents.vector: Manipulation of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (Rockwell/Allen-Bradley and Unitronics) at water, energy and municipal sites since at least March.
incidents.impact: Six US federal agencies (FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, Cyber Command) issued a joint advisory; victim organizations confirmed operational disruptions and financial losses. One IRGC-linked group paused US attacks at the ceasefire but vowed to resume.

incidents.vector: Spearphishing and social-engineering links driving users to malicious external sites, plus creation of test accounts and groups on WhatsApp.
incidents.impact: Meta says NSO Group ran spyware-linked attacks against WhatsApp users in violation of an October court injunction; Meta filed a contempt-of-court complaint. Activity resembled prior 1-click campaigns that hit journalists and activists.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (npm, PyPI, Red Hat namespace)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating Shai-Hulud/Miasma/Hades worm abuses npm install hooks and Python .pth startup files, installing a Bun-powered stealer that harvests cloud, CI/CD, GitHub and SSH secrets then republishes poisoned packages.
incidents.impact: Latest 'Hades' wave hit 37 PyPI wheels across 19 packages; a June 1 wave trojanized 32 packages in the @redhat-cloud-services namespace (~80K weekly downloads) via a compromised Red Hat GitHub account. Credential rotation urged for any install environment.

incidents.vector: Eight-month 'Matryoshka'/Doppelganger campaign of fabricated news, manipulated videos, bot amplification and impersonated outlets, plus fake bomb threats to polling stations.
incidents.impact: One of the largest Russia-linked disinformation campaigns observed; aimed to undermine PM Pashinyan's pro-European party, which still won ~50% of the vote. Bomb hoaxes from foreign numbers disrupted several polling stations.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — phishing and initial-access brokers
incidents.vector: Phishing, malvertising and SEO abuse impersonating AI brands (ChatGPT, Claude/Anthropic, Copilot, DeepSeek) using multi-hop redirect chains, CAPTCHA gating and AiTM kits to steal credentials, card data and tokens.
incidents.impact: Microsoft tracked AI-themed campaigns including a ChatGPT-billing lure (up to 100K emails/day) harvesting card data and a Claude 'AUP appeal' lure targeting 2,000+ organizations for AiTM token theft; some delivered Vidar stealer via Storm-3075/Fox Tempest.

incidents.vector: Claimed network intrusion and data exfiltration; details unverified.
incidents.impact: A group calling itself 'APT Iran' claimed to be selling exfiltrated Lockheed Martin data, including purported F-35 blueprints, for over $598 million. Claim is unverified but fits a pattern of multiyear Iranian espionage against Western aerospace and defense.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto PAN-OS / GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication-bypass flaw in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal/gateway that lets unauthorized attackers establish VPN sessions.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and some successful gateway-connected sessions; no post-access lateral movement yet identified. Added to CISA's KEV catalog May 29; patching and IOC hunting advised.

incidents.vector: Operation FlutterBridge: Google Ads from shell companies push Flutter-built apps (podcast/PDF tools) carrying the FlutterShell backdoor, which uses a WebView JavaScript-to-native bridge for remote command execution and file theft.
incidents.impact: Notarized, Apple-signed samples with zero VirusTotal detections hijack Chrome and add backdoor capabilities including AI-summarization-based data exfiltration. Google suspended the advertiser accounts; malware under active development.

incidents.vector: Smart-contract abuse: unauthorized token minting/dumping (TesseraDAO) and draining of a central airdrop wallet (SuperFortune), with proceeds laundered via cross-chain bridges and Tornado Cash.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole roughly $2.5 million from TesseraDAO and about $15 million from SuperFortune; both platforms are still investigating.
Password manager Dashlane disclosed that a brute-force attack resulted in the theft of nearly 20 encrypted password vaults; the company published a technical post-mortem.

incidents.victim: Instagram (incl. Obama White House, US Space Force accounts)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering of Meta's AI support assistant: using a local-area VPN and the bot's password-reset flow to link an attacker email and trigger a one-time reset code, bypassing weak account recovery.
incidents.impact: High-value Instagram accounts including the Obama White House and the Space Force Chief Master Sergeant were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian messages; hackers claimed to seize short usernames worth over $500K. Meta pushed an emergency patch; MFA-protected accounts were unaffected.

incidents.vector: A poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (v18.95.0, CVE-2026-48027) distributed via auto-update compromised a GitHub employee device; the separate 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Action workflows to harvest CI/CD secrets and cloud tokens.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access and exfiltration of internal GitHub repositories; Megalodon backdoored numerous public repos to steal credentials. CISA added the CVE to KEV and urged secret rotation and workflow audits.

incidents.vector: Use of compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data.
incidents.impact: Roughly 600,000 records stolen, including real names, cadastral and property information.

incidents.vector: Data theft and extortion; victim named on the actor's dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: US telecom Charter confirmed a security breach after being listed on the ShinyHunters leak site.

incidents.vector: Data-theft intrusion attributed to the ShinyHunters group.
incidents.impact: American cruise operator Carnival disclosed another security incident, the latest caused by ShinyHunters.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion with data theft for extortion leverage.
incidents.impact: The Play ransomware group is extorting MyPillow, claiming theft of sensitive financial documents from its corporate network. The company has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Misconfigured, non-official immigration website exposing applicant data publicly.
incidents.impact: More than 100,000 documents, including selfies and passport scans, were leaking from an unofficial UK visa portal, which had not fixed the exposure.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and staff
incidents.vector: Compromise of WhatsApp accounts, believed to be part of a broader campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: A suspected foreign state actor breached the WhatsApp account of independent MP Zali Steggall and three staffers in March; attribution to a Russian campaign is unconfirmed.
